hints.title: Where to look
hints.body: Look at `renderCommentHtml()` in `src/comments.js`. It builds an HTML string and interpolates `comment.author` and `comment.text` directly into the template. Try passing `author = ''` and see what the output HTML looks like.

hints.title: The concept
hints.body: This is a **reflected / stored XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)** vulnerability caused by **missing output encoding**. User-controlled strings are concatenated directly into HTML without escaping the five special characters (`& < > " '`). Any attacker who can store a comment can inject arbitrary HTML or JavaScript that executes in victims' browsers when the preview is rendered.

hints.title: The fix approach
hints.body: Write an `escapeHtml(str)` helper that replaces the five special characters with their HTML entities: ``` & → & < → < > → > " → " ' → ' ``` Call `escapeHtml(comment.author)` and `escapeHtml(comment.text)` before interpolating into the template string. **Do NOT** store escaped text — escape at the *output boundary* only, so the raw text remains reusable.
